In the context of Artificial Intelligence, particularly in the field of natural language processing (NLP), "Transformers" refer to a type of deep learning model architecture that has revolutionized the way machines understand and generate human language. The Transformer model was introduced in a 2017 paper titled "Attention is All You Need" by researchers at Google Brain and other institutions.

The key innovation of the Transformer model is the self-attention mechanism, which allows the model to weigh the importance of different words in a sentence when processing it. This mechanism enables the model to handle long-range dependencies in text more effectively than previous models, such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and long short-term memory networks (LSTMs).

Transformers have several advantages:
1. **Parallelization**: Unlike RNNs, which process sequences one element at a time, Transformers can process all elements of a sequence in parallel, making them much faster to train.
2. **Scalability**: Transformers can be scaled up to handle very large datasets and can be trained on massive amounts of text data, leading to better performance on a wide range of NLP tasks.
3. **Flexibility**: The Transformer architecture can be adapted to a variety of tasks, including translation, text summarization, question answering, and more.

Since their introduction, Transformers have become the backbone of many state-of-the-art NLP models, including BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer), and T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer), among others. These models have significantly advanced the field of NLP and have applications in a wide range of industries, from customer service chatbots to medical research.
